newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia in pact to market cervical test.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia in pact to market cervical test.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc. has agreed to jointly market in the United States a cervical screening test by Trylon Corp. that enhances the effectivesness of the traditional Pap smear test, the companies said Thursday.

The test, Trylon's first product, significantly improves the sensitivity of the cervical screening exam in finding abnormalities compared with using a Pap smear alone, they said. The combination was tested in clinical trials involving more than 10,000 women.

The test combines a patented visual examination technique called speculoscopy with the standard Pap smear into a simple cervical screening test. It features a chemical light that allows physicians to identify possible abnormalities during a routine cervical exam.
The product is now being disributed in Canada and in certain European and Asian markets through other pharmaceutical and medical supply companies.
Trylon is a privately held company based in Torrance, Calif.
Kalamazoo, Mich.-based Pharmacia & Upjohn's stock edged down 37.5 cents to $38.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
